messages.author: 4778dcdaf4dfb3fb
messages.subject: Strip labels in grid layout?
parts:
Greetings ggplotters!

I'm new to the package, but finding it (and this message board) very
useful. Right now, I wish to place 5 plots on one page. These are
plots of odds ratios and (non-symmetrical) confidence intervals.
Faceting has some desirable results that I hope to preserve in a grid
layout.

Here's an approximation of my data and the facet grid:

library(ggplot2)

dframe<-
data.frame(group=rep(LETTERS[1:5],each=3),variable=rep(LETTERS[24:26],times=5),OR=rnorm(15,5),lower=rnorm(15,1),upper=rnorm(15,8))
dframe[4:6,3:5]<-dframe[4:6,3:5]+50 # some of the effects in my data
are on very different scales


p<-ggplot(data=dframe,aes(x=variable,y=OR))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)

p+geom_point(data=dframe,aes(y=OR))
+geom_linerange(data=dframe,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))+coord_flip()
+ylab('Odds Ratio')+xlab(NULL)+facet_grid(group~.)




#The facet gives nice strip labels that identify the group, but
because the # scales are very different and I wish to emphasize the
first of #the plots (group A), I've gone to a grid layout.



#now I subset to make 5 new plots for use in a grid layout

A<-subset(dframe,group=='A')

B<-subset(dframe,group=='B')

C<-subset(dframe,group=='C')

D<-subset(dframe,group=='D')

E<-subset(dframe,group=='E')

pA<-ggplot(data=A,aes(x=variable))+geom_point(data=A,aes(y=OR))
+coord_flip()+geom_linerange(data=A,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)+xlab(NULL)+ylab(NULL)
+opts(plot.margin=unit(rep(.5,4),'lines'))

pB<-ggplot(data=B,aes(x=variable))+geom_point(data=B,aes(y=OR))
+coord_flip()+geom_linerange(data=B,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)+xlab(NULL)+ylab(NULL)
+opts(plot.margin=unit(rep(.5,4),'lines'))

pC<-ggplot(data=C,aes(x=variable))+geom_point(data=C,aes(y=OR))
+coord_flip()+geom_linerange(data=C,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)+xlab(NULL)+ylab(NULL)
+opts(plot.margin=unit(rep(.5,4),'lines'))

pD<-ggplot(data=D,aes(x=variable))+geom_point(data=D,aes(y=OR))
+coord_flip()+geom_linerange(data=D,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)+xlab(NULL)+ylab(NULL)
+opts(plot.margin=unit(rep(.5,4),'lines'))

pE<-ggplot(data=E,aes(x=variable))+geom_point(data=E,aes(y=OR))
+coord_flip()+geom_linerange(data=E,aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper))
+geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1)+xlab(NULL)+ylab(NULL)
+opts(plot.margin=unit(rep(.5,4),'lines'))


pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(3,2)))
vplayout<-function(x,y) viewport(layout.pos.row =x, layout.pos.col=y)

print(pA,vp=vplayout(1,1:2))
print(pB,vp=vplayout(2,1))
print(pC,vp=vplayout(3,1))
print(pD,vp=vplayout(2,2))
print(pE,vp=vplayout(3,2))



Sorry for my inelegant coding; as I said, I'm a ggplot novice.
Anyways, this approach allows the scales to vary and provides labels
on each axis. I would love to add the strip labels that are present in
the faceted plots to the grid layout plots. Is there any way to do
this? Barring that, I guess I'll add some text to identify each plot.
I haven't spent time figuring out how to do that, so suggestions are
welcome.

As an aside, does anyone see a way I could have plotted the points and
lines in this manner with needing to use coord_flip?

Many thanks,

Justin

messages.author: 539623a2f30c9e53
messages.subject: Re: Strip labels in grid layout?
parts:
Maybe facet_wrap?

[...] + facet_wrap(~ g, ncol=1, scale="free")

Note that facet_wrap throws an error if your faceting variable is
called "group", so I shortened it to "g".

Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: Strip labels in grid layout?
parts:
my.theme.title <- function(label, ..., vjust = 0.5,
hjust = 0.5, default.units = "npc") {
tg <- textGrob(label, unit(0.5,"npc"), unit(0.5,"npc") + unit(0.25,"lines"),
hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust, ...,
default.units = default.units)
rg <- rectGrob(x=1, height=unit(1,"lines"), just="right",
y=unit(0.5,"npc") + unit(0.25,"lines"),
width=unit(1,"npc")-unit(1, "lines"),
gp=gpar(fill="grey80",col=NA))

gTree(children=gList(rg,tg))
}


p <- ggplot(data=dframe, aes(x=variable)) + geom_point(aes(y=OR)) +
coord_flip() + geom_linerange(aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper)) +
geom_hline(yintercept=1,linetype=2,size=0.1) + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) +
opts(plot.title = my.theme.title,
plot.margin = unit(c(1,0.5,0.5,0.5), "lines"))

all.plots <- dlply(dframe, .(group),
function(.d) { p %+% .d +
opts(title = unique(.d$group))})

## all.plots[[1]]

library(gridExtra)

## basic layout
## do.call(grid.arrange, all.plots)

## trick to have the first plot full width
do.call(grid.arrange,
list(all.plots[[1]], do.call(arrangeGrob, all.plots[-1]), ncol=1))


HTH,

baptiste
